name: Gregory B Maffei
current_role: Executive Chairman, QVC Group; Chairman of SiriusXM and Tripadvisor; President & CEO, Liberty TripAdvisor (former Liberty Media CEO 2005-2025)
profile: Greg Maffei ran Liberty Media and the Liberty family of companies (Formula One, SiriusXM, Atlanta Braves, Liberty Broadband/Charter stake) as president and CEO from 2005 until stepping down at end-2024, staying on as a senior adviser. Earlier he was Microsoft CFO (1997-99), chairman of Expedia, CEO of 360networks and briefly Oracle president/CFO.
interesting_fact: He was CFO of Microsoft (1997-1999) and later spent just four months as Oracle's president and CFO in 2005 before joining John Malone at Liberty Media.
deep_cut_fact: He was a Baker Scholar at Harvard Business School, served as president of the board of trustees of the Seattle Public Library, and was vice chair of Dartmouth College's Board of Trustees.
notes: Announced Nov 2024 he would step down as Liberty Media CEO at year-end; Derek Chang succeeded him Feb 2025. Sources differ on his exact 2026 board portfolio (some list Live Nation chair, Charter director) - verify via latest proxy filings. Route via Liberty/QVC Group investor relations. Telecom/cable background (360networks fiber, Charter) relevant to data-center angle.

name: Li Yinhui
current_role: Chairman, Qinghai Huzhu Tianyoude Highland Barley Spirit Co. (天佑德酒, SZSE 002646)
profile: Li Yinhui (李银会), born 1966 in Shanxi, studied geology at Peking University, then sold computers for Huaneng in northwest China and in 1994 founded a computer business in Xining. He went on to buy over ten state firms and in 2005 acquired the struggling Qinghai Huzhu barley-liquor factory, built the Tianyoude brand and listed it in 2011. He chaired the new 6th board in March 2026.
interesting_fact: His company listed on 22 Dec 2011 as China's first highland-barley liquor stock, backed by an organic barley base of around 100,000 mu in Qinghai.
deep_cut_fact: A Shanxi native who got into Peking University's geology department at 17, he started out after graduating in 1990 selling computers for state-owned Huaneng Group, opening up the Qinghai market, before founding his own computer store in Xining in 1994.
notes: Current chairmanship confirmed by SZSE board announcement (https://paper.cnstock.com/html/2026-03/18/content_2189467.htm). Bio details come from a promotional Sina feature; reported to have donated 10m+ yuan to education in Yuncheng. Route via company board secretary.

name: Akshata Murty
current_role: Director, Catamaran Ventures (venture capital); Infosys shareholder (~0.9%)
profile: Akshata Murty, born 1980 in Hubballi, India, is the daughter of Infosys co-founder N. R. Narayana Murthy and holds roughly 0.9% of Infosys. Educated at Claremont McKenna, FIDM Los Angeles and Stanford (MBA), she ran a fashion label, became a director of Catamaran Ventures in 2013 and has stakes/board seats in businesses such as Digme Fitness and Soroco. She is married to former UK PM Rishi Sunak.
interesting_fact: She studied economics and French at Claremont McKenna, then took a diploma in clothes manufacturing at the Fashion Institute of Design and Merchandising before launching her own fashion label.
deep_cut_fact: Before fashion and venture capital, she spent two years from 2007 as marketing director at Tendris, a Dutch cleantech firm - a neat link to an energy podcast.
notes: High-profile and media-cautious given former spouse-of-PM role; no personal official site/social listed on Wikipedia. Best route likely via Catamaran Ventures or a mutual introduction. Avoid property/tax topics.

name: d'Ovidio Manfredi Lefebvre
current_role: President, Heritage Group; Executive Chairman, Abercrombie & Kent Travel Group; Vice Chairman, Arqit Quantum; Chair, World Travel & Tourism Council (since Sept 2025)
profile: Manfredi Lefebvre d'Ovidio (b. 1953) is an Italian-Monegasque businessman based in Monaco who ran Silversea Cruises, founded by his father, as chairman/executive chairman 2001-2020; Royal Caribbean bought two-thirds for about US$1bn in 2018 and later took full control. Through Heritage Group he invests in travel (Abercrombie & Kent, Crystal Cruises), property and tech, including quantum-encryption firm Arqit.
interesting_fact: After selling Silversea, his Abercrombie & Kent group bought Crystal Cruises in June 2022, and he became chair of the World Travel & Tourism Council in Sept 2025.
deep_cut_fact: He has been Honorary Consul of Ecuador in Monaco since 2019, and from 2010 chaired the European Cruise Council, helping merge it into CLIA (Cruise Lines International Association).
notes: Also a Rothschild & Co global senior advisor and president of a pediatric palliative-care foundation (Fondazione Maruzza). Arqit governance page lists him as Vice Chairman/Senior Independent Director (https://ir.arqit.uk/corporate-governance). Wikipedia references manfredilefebvre.com but its ownership was not verified.

current_role: Advisor, MPM BioImpact (co-founder of predecessor MPM Capital); board member, Werewolf Therapeutics
profile: Luke Evnin (Princeton A.B. 1985, UCSF biochemistry Ph.D. 1990) spent 1990-97 at Accel Partners, then co-founded life-sciences VC MPM Capital with Ansbert Gadicke in 1997, opening its San Francisco office in 1999. He co-founded and chaired biotechs including Harpoon, Maverick (sold to Takeda), Potenza (Astellas) and Werewolf, where he was interim CEO 2017-19. He is now an advisor at MPM BioImpact.

name: Graeme Brooks
current_role: Founder and CEO, Avtrade (aircraft spare parts and component support, West Sussex, UK)
profile: Graeme Brooks founded Avtrade in 1985 with former boss Fred Dunn, starting out trading Boeing 737 rotables from his home in the UK. After the pair split business interests amicably in 1993 he built Avtrade into a global Airbus/Boeing parts and AOG logistics supplier with offices in Beijing, France, Singapore and Dubai and a purpose-built UK HQ (2005). He and Yvonne Brooks are listed as persons with significant control.
interesting_fact: Avtrade was born over a drink in London in 1985, when Brooks and his then-boss at Miami parts dealer Aerosystems, Fred Dunn, decided they could do it themselves; the two remained lifelong friends after splitting the business in 1993.
deep_cut_fact: He left home at 15 and got his first job in the purchasing department of British Caledonian Airways at Gatwick, later rising to VP of Sales for Europe at Aerosystems before founding Avtrade.
notes: Company history page signs off as 'Graeme Brooks CEO' (alive assumed from current company messaging). PSC per Companies House (https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/01917328/persons-with-significant-control). Private, low media profile; route via Avtrade.
